title: Rational polyhedral cones have finite rational half-space descriptions
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q$-vector space [def-weil-field] [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], let $v_1,\ldots,v_m\in V$ (allowing $m=0$), and put $C=\{\sum_j q_jv_j:q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\}$. Then there are finitely many $\mathbf Q$-linear forms $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s:V\to\mathbf Q$ (allowing $s=0$) such that $$C=\{x\in V:\lambda_i(x)\ge0\text{ for every }i\}.$$ This is the rational Minkowski--Weyl (finite H-cone) description; no pointedness or spanning hypothesis is required.

source.place: Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, rational polyhedral-cone description; Kato 1994, Toric singularities, is WANTED for a proof of the finite rational half-space form.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], choose a finite spanning list in $V$. Repeatedly remove an element expressible as a linear combination of the others; the span is unchanged and the list strictly shortens. The resulting list $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ is linearly independent: any nontrivial relation, solved for a vector with nonzero coefficient, would allow another removal. It is therefore a basis. For $x=\sum_h x_he_h$ let $\epsilon_h(x)=x_h$. Uniqueness of coordinates shows $\epsilon_h(x+y)=\epsilon_h(x)+\epsilon_h(y)$ and $\epsilon_h(qx)=q\epsilon_h(x)$, so these are rational linear forms. Their signed family $\{\epsilon_h,-\epsilon_h:1\le h\le n\}$ has nonnegative locus $\{0\}$, because both signs force every coordinate to be zero. For $V=0$ this family is empty.

source.place: Agent-written proof, base family: finite coordinates and the zero cone. Remark 3.1.29 is contextual only and does not contain this argument.

proof.text: For $0\le k\le m$ put $C_k=\{\sum_{j=1}^k q_jv_j:q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\}$. We prove by induction on $k$ that $C_k$ is the nonnegative locus of a finite family of rational linear forms. The preceding signed coordinate family gives the base case $C_0=\{0\}$. For the induction step, suppose $C_k=\{x:f_i(x)\ge0\ (i\in I)\}$ for a finite index set $I$, and put $v=v_{k+1}$. Splitting off the last coefficient gives $$x\in C_{k+1}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists t\in\mathbf Q,\ t\ge0\ \text{and}\ f_i(x)-t f_i(v)\ge0\ (i\in I).$$ Indeed the old inequalities say exactly that $x-tv\in C_k$.

source.place: Agent-written proof, induction assertion, base case and coefficient identity. Remark 3.1.29 is contextual only and does not contain this argument.

proof.text: The induction hypothesis makes $I$ finite. Apply [lem-trf-rational-ray-elimination-forward] to the finite family $f_i$ and $v$. It supplies the finite rational-linear family $\mathcal F$ consisting of the zero-sign forms, positive-sign forms and $g_{ij}=a_i f_j-a_j f_i$ for $i\in I_+$ and $j\in I_-$, where $a_i=f_i(v)$. Every witness $t$ in Step 2 makes every member nonnegative. Thus $C_{k+1}$ is contained in its nonnegative locus.

source.place: Agent-written auxiliary assertion extracted from lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite, old proof steps 3--4 (explicit finite family and forward inclusion). Expose VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, supplies toric context only, not this assertion.

proof.text: For the reverse inclusion, assume every member of $\mathcal F$ is nonnegative at $x$. Put $a_i=f_i(v)$ and $b_i=f_i(x)$. The retained forms give $b_h\ge0$ on $I_0$ and $b_i\ge0$ on $I_+$; evaluation gives $g_{ij}(x)=a_i b_j-a_j b_i\ge0$ on $I_+\times I_-$. Thus [lem-trf-rational-ray-elimination-witness] applies to the same finite $I$. Its $B=\{0\}\cup\{b_j/a_j:j\in I_-\}$ has a rational maximum $T\ge0$ with $b_i-Ta_i\ge0$ for all $i$. Since $f_i(x-Tv)=b_i-Ta_i$, the induction hypothesis gives $x-Tv\in C_k$, and Step 2 gives $x\in C_{k+1}$.

source.place: Agent-written auxiliary assertion extracted from lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite, old proof step 5 and step 6 empty-sign-class discussion. Expose VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, supplies toric context only, not this assertion.

proof.text: Steps 3--4 complete the induction. At $k=m$, enumerate the final finite family as $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s$; its nonnegative locus is $C_m=C$. All operations are rational, and divisions use only strictly signed $a_i$. Empty sign classes are allowed: $I_-=\varnothing$ gives $B=\{0\}$ and $T=0$, while $I_+=\varnothing$ imposes no upper bounds. If the old family is empty, both old and new cones are $V$. For $m=0$ use the signed coordinate family; for $V=0$ use the empty family. No pointedness or spanning assumption on the generators was used.
